title: Shortburst signal probe — heuristic log (Harriet)
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for a ‘shortburst’ probe workflow — small, repeatable micro-evals intended to catch transient/regression signals that show up only in narrow time slices or when prefix caching + quantized kernels interact. Not intended as a replacement for full eval suites; meant to be cheap, fast, and noisy by design.

Background/context:
- Noticed a couple of customer reports last week where short inputs (<=12 tokens) suddenly produced very long-winded completions after a rollout to q4-optim kernels. Root cause hypothesis: subtle change in prefix handling in batched KV cache path + tokenization edge case for punctuation.
- Full regression tests (large eval set) didn’t catch it because it emerges only with low-token prompts and ~3-4 concurrent streams.

This doc: notes + example prompts, observed outputs, quick ad-hoc rubric, and next steps. Iterate here then move to a tiny reproducible test in CI.

1) Quick probe recipe (how to run a shortburst)
- Pick 10 seed prompts: short, ambiguous, punctuation-heavy, few-shot with 1 example.
- Run on: control (pre-rollout binary), new binary (q4-optim), and fallback (gpu-compat).
- Run N=200 fast micro-requests per binary, concurrency=3, sequence_limit=64, temperature=0.0 and 0.7.
- Capture: latency, top-k tokens, final length, first-10-tokens of completion, and whether a ‘looping’ token pattern appears.

2) Seed prompts (examples used in probe)
- "Translate: Hola."
- "Q: 2+2 ="
- "Summarize: Hello?"
- "List: apple,"
- "Instruction: reply briefly."
- "Ticket: error 503."
- "Email: Thanks,."
- "Do: write a title"
- "Code: def f():\n"
- "Prompt: "Who" said it?"

3) Observed anomalies (run 2025-11-03)
- Control (v23.4)
  - Mostly expected: short completions, many <12 tokens.
- New binary (q4-optim)
  - ~18% of runs for prompts with trailing punctuation produced completions that repeated fragments and expanded to >60 tokens.
  - Pattern: when prompt ended with ambiguous punctuation ("Hello?", "Thanks,.") model generated an opening paragraph repeated twice then a trailing apology.
  - Concurrency effect: anomaly rate increased to ~30% when concurrent streams=3-4 vs 1.
- Fallback (gpu-compat)
  - Rare anomalies (~2%), similar to control.

4) Sample problematic interaction (raw)
- Prompt: "Summarize: Hello?"
- Control output: "Hello is a greeting. In brief, ..." (8 tokens)
- New binary output: "Hello is a greeting. In brief,... Hello is a greeting. In brief,... Sorry about that." (repeated paragraph)
- Quick note: repetition appears at sentence-boundary tokens (period, question) and sometimes when tokenizer produces an extra empty token for trailing punctuation.

5) Ad-hoc rubric (4-point quick scale per sample)
- 0 = correct length, coherent, no repetition
- 1 = minor verbosity (10–30% longer), acceptable
- 2 = excessive verbosity or mild repetition (30–100% longer)
- 3 = clear repetition/loop or incoherent expansion (>100% longer)

6) Quick scoring summary (seed set, 200 runs each)
- Control: mean score 0.3, median 0, p95 1
- New binary: mean score 1.1, median 1, p95 2.5 (spike on punctuation cases)
- Fallback: mean 0.4, median 0, p95 1

7) Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: KV cache pointer drift under specific kernel scheduling leads to partial re-injection of prefix for short prompts when tokenized trailing punctuation produces zero-length token. (High priority)
- H2: A change in fused-attention ordering causes some attention slot to be read twice at concurrency >1. (Medium)
- H3: New tokenization post-processing (edge-case trimming) mislabels trailing punctuation tokens as separate units, causing the model to interpret as two prompts and produce two completions. (Low-medium)

8) Quick experiments to triangulate (do these in parallel)
- Deterministic token-level trace: record tokenizer output for offending prompts across kernels. If tokens differ, H3 gain credence.
- Cache-eviction toggle: run with cache disabled; if regression disappears, H1 likely.
- Single-stream vs multi: sweep concurrency from 1..8 and plot anomaly rate.
- Tiny reproducible harness: seed=42, temperature=0.0, limit=64, single prompt repeated 1000x with inter-request gap 20ms.

9) Notes from Marco (inline Slack copy)
- "I ran trace on the kv pointers — saw off-by-one on read index in q4-optim. Will drop patch to CI. Might explain double-read."

10) Quick action items (short-term)
- [ ] Reproduce locally with cache disabled (Harriet) — due 2025-11-06
- [ ] Add microtest that runs seed prompts with concurrency sweep (PR to serving-runtime/e2e) — assignee: Marco
- [ ] Add tokenizer golden-check against control (Anya) — due 2025-11-07
- [ ] If KV patch reduces anomaly, schedule small canary roll with increased sampling.

11) Long-term notes (rambling)
- Consider adding a small synthetic shortburst harness to our daily canary pipeline. It only needs 100 fast requests per binary per day, focused on punctuation/whitespace edge cases.
- Flag: make sure to collect token-level traces by default for shortburst runs — will be invaluable.

12) Misc observations and fuzzy thoughts
- This whole class of bugs disproportionately affects user-facing tiny prompts (chat UI quick replies, email subject generation). Customers notice more because it feels jarring.
- If this is KV-cache related, it could also cause subtle hallucination in rare cases when prefix tokens are doubled.

End notes: keep this doc as a moving scratchpad. If/when we have a minimal CI test, move to confluence shortburst page and link here.

Recent edits: 2025-11-05 — added scoring summary and action items after Marco's trace note.
